leads.summary: The VM hardening is only preflight: an empty shared directory returns to mode 2777 when the guest starts
leads.consequence: For an empty ~/Windows, the new chmod 00700 restores 700 before starting Docker, but the container's Samba setup explicitly chmods the empty writable /shared to 2777 during startup. The host directory is again readable and writable by other local accounts while the VM is running and stays so after stop until another privileged/user prepare runs. The new tests only check the mode before Docker starts, never after actual Samba initialization. This is a limitation of the security fix, not a newly introduced exposure. An after-start re-hardening path or documented limitation would be needed for an end-to-end privacy promise; independent PR #9783 proposes such a path.
leads.triage: dropped; Dockurr resetting the share to 2777 after start is pre-existing and concerns only the unrelated VM commit, which the comment suggests dropping.

leads.summary: Open #13478 shares this PR's Windows VM parent commit and conflicts with its BarModel addition
leads.consequence: The two PR heads diverge after the *same* parent commit 2b4b0eba, which accounts for their identical VM modifications. Three-way merge at the common base places isRealScreen/realScreens and notchHeight at the same insertion location in BarModel.js, yielding conflict markers at merged BarModel.js:211-280. Until resolved, neither combined bar feature nor the other PR's notch fixture can be used. Preserve both exported helpers when resolving, and coordinate the shared unrelated VM prerequisite; separate PR #13213 independently covers that correction.
leads.triage: confirmed_not_published; Verified with git merge-file (coord/x1/merged.js lines 211-280): add/add conflict at the end of BarModel.js with #13478 (same author). Trivial to resolve; not material.

leads.summary: Open #13165 is an almost identical independent bar fix, including a test-file merge conflict
leads.consequence: The heads are diverged, but their Bar.qml changes and filter implementations are functionally the same. Three-way merge retains both bar changes without duplication, while whitespace differences after the added tests cause two conflict hunks in bar-test.sh. Coordinate/close the duplicate or resolve those test hunks if either merges first; this is integration/maintenance, not an additional runtime bug.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; Same as Opus F1 (#13165 duplicate).

leads.summary: Open #13213 implements the same setgid fix in the same VM command
leads.consequence: #13213 (diverged, not stacked) has identical chmod 00700 replacements at both production sites and a more direct root-side writer fixture. Three-way merge leaves identical production behaviour but produces two comment conflicts in omarchy-windows-vm and a conflict between the competing fixtures. Treat the unrelated Windows commit as a duplicate fix and coordinate with #13213 before merging rather than carrying two copies into a bar PR.

leads.summary: Open #10113 would restore launch from a world-writable shared source instead of enforcing this PR's 700-mode boundary
leads.consequence: The two heads are diverged and merge-file produces two real conflicts at the root-mode preflight, plus #10113 changes mounted_leaf_matches to accept modes 2777/2700. If the conflicts are resolved by retaining #10113's permissive mounted_leaf_matches, a sudoless-Docker user whose guest left ~/Windows at 2777 passes mounts_ready and the direct __priv_up_wait path: no root prepare_caller_mounts runs, so the new 00700 hardening is skipped. This is #10113's explicitly stated tradeoff to make headless launches work, not an accidental defect in that PR; maintainers must choose whether a mode-700 privacy invariant or its 2777-tolerant startup behaviour wins. #10113's test asserting mounts_ready accepts 2777 fails if this PR's exact guard is retained.
leads.triage: dropped; #10113 accepting 2777 concerns only the VM commit; out of proportion for a bar PR comment.

leads.summary: The screen filter does not cover other panel IPC handlers implicated by #13072
leads.consequence: The filter only controls the built-in bar's three Variants. In #13072, the reporter listed duplicate IpcHandler registrations in standalone agents, bluetooth, network, audio, monitor, power and weather panels and a leaked third-party plugin child after wake. The agents IpcHandler is a separate component and notifications/background still use raw Quickshell.screens, so claiming this fully fixes that issue would exceed what the changed files do. It may prevent extra bar widgets/ghosts but does not independently tear down stale plugin or panel instances.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus_partly_wrong; Partial-fix framing matches Opus F3. Claim that the agents IPC handler is independent of the bar is wrong: shell/plugins/agents/manifest.json lists Panel.qml as the barWidget entry point. Not published.

leads.summary: Both changed VM mount tests can report success without exercising either added chmod assertion
leads.consequence: Where unprivileged user/mount namespaces or subordinate IDs are unavailable, each script exits with status 0 via pass(...skipping...) before reaching the new runtime assertions. The separate windows-vm-test.sh grep assertion proves the literal spelling chmod 00700, and its mktemp-dir probe proves generic coreutils behavior, but neither verifies the actual VM call path. A broken implementation that leaves runtime directories at 2700 after chmod would escape these tests on such a CI worker. Make the suite report a skip rather than a success and require a capability-enabled run for boundary coverage.
leads.triage: dropped; VM fixture fallback 'pass' is pre-existing and already changed to 'skip' on quattro.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the bar filter does what the description says, and existing bars are not rebuilt when the filtered list is recomputed.

| Screen | Name | Size | Gets a bar |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qt placeholder (no outputs) | `""` | 0x0 | no |
| Hyprland `FALLBACK` | `FALLBACK` | 1920x1080 | no (name check only) |
| Real monitor reported at 0x0 (defensive case, checked with a stand-in) | `DP-1` | 0x0 | not yet; gets one when its size arrives |
| Real monitor / user headless output | `HDMI-A-1` / `HEADLESS-2` | real mode | yes |

- In the dependency sources, Qt's placeholder screen has an empty name and empty geometry. Hyprland 0.56.2 advertises `FALLBACK` as an ordinary `wl_output` at 1920x1080, so only the name check excludes it. Qt Wayland names a real screen before adding it, so a real screen never reaches the filter without a name. A size that arrives or changes later is still tracked by the binding.
- A headless Quickshell run with this `BarModel.js`, a `realScreens` binding and a `Variants` over stand-in screen objects behaved as follows. A screen whose size arrived later got an instance. A resolution change, and the placeholder and `FALLBACK` leaving the list, did not rebuild existing instances. `Variants` compares the same screen object as equal across recomputations.
- `bar-test.sh` passes on this head and with the head merged into current `quattro`. Its new checks fail with the merge-base `Bar.qml`/`BarModel.js`, without the `FALLBACK` check, without the geometry check, or with one `Variants` reverted.

The review found an overlap with an open PR, an unrelated Windows VM commit, a "Fixes" link that covers only part of #13072, and a test guard that passes on zero matches.

### Same change as open PR #13165

#13165 ("Skip placeholder screens when building bars", open since 24 Sep) makes the same bar change:
- `Bar.qml` after this PR is byte-identical to `Bar.qml` at #13165's head.
- `isRealScreen`/`realScreens` in `BarModel.js` are character-identical. Here they sit at the end of the file with a reworded comment.
- The `bar-test.sh` assertions are the same. This PR only adds blank lines around them.

**Impact:** there are two open PRs with the same bar code, linking different issues (#13072 here, #13163 there).

**Suggested change:** state what this PR adds over #13165, or consolidate the change in one PR.

### Unrelated Windows VM commit

Commit `2b4b0eba` ("Clear setgid when hardening Windows VM mount folders (#1)") changes `bin/omarchy-windows-vm` and three tests. The description does not mention it, and it is unrelated to the bar. The same commit is also in #13473, #13478 and #13480. Dedicated PRs with the same `chmod 00700` are open as well (#13213 at both sites, #13154 at the caller-mount site), along with others that use a symbolic mode (for example #12323).

**Verified:** the fix itself is correct. With GNU chmod 9.11, `chmod 0700` on a 2777 directory leaves 2700 and `chmod 00700` gives 700, also through `/proc/PID/fd`. The new `windows-vm-compose-test.sh` case fails when the old line is restored.

**Impact:** the same unrelated change travels in several open PRs alongside the dedicated ones. Once one lands, the others become redundant or conflict at the same lines.

**Suggested change:** drop the commit from this PR. If it stays, the comments "Use a leading 0 in the mode" and "Leading 0 clears setuid/setgid" are imprecise, because `0700` already has a leading zero. What matters is the fifth digit (`00700`).

### "Fixes #13072" covers only part of the issue

```text
all outputs drop
  ├─ placeholder / FALLBACK bar            -> no longer built (this PR)
  ├─ real monitor's bar                    -> still destroyed, rebuilt when outputs return
  └─ background, notification windows      -> still created for every Quickshell.screens entry,
                                              placeholder included (Background.qml:210,
                                              notifications/Service.qml:953)
```

With the filter, no bar, bar widgets or widget IPC handlers are built for the placeholder or `FALLBACK`. The real monitor's bar is still removed from `Variants` when its screen leaves `Quickshell.screens`, and it is rebuilt when the screen returns. A widget that leaves a process behind on teardown can therefore still do so once per cycle. This would apply to the third-party plugin case in #13072 if its process outlives the widget's teardown; that plugin's code was not examined. The background window is always mapped, so the "Layershell screen does not correspond to a real screen" warning in #13072's log is still expected.

**Impact:** "Fixes #13072" would close an issue that the change resolves only partly.

**Suggested change:** use "Refs #13072", or state the partial scope in the description.

### Count guard passes when nothing matches

`test/shell.d/bar-test.sh:28` runs `(( $(rg -c 'model:\s*root\.realScreens' ...) != 3 ))`. When `rg` finds nothing it prints nothing, so this becomes `(( != 3 ))`. That is an arithmetic syntax error, the `if` condition is false, and the script continues even under `set -euo pipefail`.

A diagnostic mutant pointed all three `Variants` at an unfiltered `readonly property var barScreens: Quickshell.screens` and kept the `realScreens` line. `bar-test.sh` still exited 0 with 97 checks, and the only sign of the problem was the syntax error on stderr. Open PR #6501 changes these same three models to `root.barScreens`, so a conflict resolution in its favour on those three lines could drop the filter without failing this test.

**Optional test improvement:** default the count to 0. This version fails for the mutant above and passes on this head:

```bash
real_screen_models=$(rg -c 'model:\s*root\.realScreens' "$ROOT/shell/plugins/bar/Bar.qml" || true)
if (( ${real_screen_models:-0} != 3 )); then
```

**Smaller note:** the description says 98 assertions pass. This head prints 97 `ok` lines.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the head, merge-base and current `quattro`, plus Quickshell 0.3.1, Qt 6.11.2 Wayland, Hyprland 0.56.2, and open PRs #13165, #6501 and the Windows VM setgid PRs. `bar-test.sh`, `windows-vm-test.sh`, `windows-vm-compose-test.sh` (with a synthetic account entry) and diagnostic mutants ran in an isolated sandbox on this head, the merge-base, and the head merged into `quattro`. GNU chmod 9.11 behaviour was checked by running it there. Screen handling was checked with a headless Quickshell run over stand-in screen objects. No compositor, real monitors or hotplug were available, so the unplug and replug sequence itself was not observed. `windows-vm-mount-boundary-test.sh` could not run in the sandbox.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
